answer: Miscellaneous >> Dua (Supplications) Question ID: 3384 Country: Pakistan Title: I would be grateful if you could answer a couple of quick questions for me. I am a chartered accountant from Lahore, Pakistan. My mother is suffering from decompensated liver cirrhosis, and she also has hepatitis C. Is there any dua we should read or any other diet you would recommend on basis of Quran/hadith? Also is it against Islam to visit people 1) who proclaim to cure people by reading verses from the Quran or 2) who proclaim that they are blessed with healing powers. If this is ok in Islam, then would you know of any one? I understand that you are very busy, but would be extremely grateful for an early reply. Question: Assasalmalaikum, I would be grateful if you could answer a couple of quick questions for me. I am a chartered accountant from Lahore, Pakistan. My mother is suffering from decompensated liver cirrhosis, and she also has hepatitis C. Is there any dua we should read or any other diet you would recommend on basis of Quran/hadith? Also is it against Islam to visit people 1) who proclaim to cure people by reading verses from the Quran or 2) who proclaim that they are blessed with healing powers. If this is ok in Islam, then would you know of any one? I understand that you are very busy, but would be extremely grateful for an early reply. Thanks! Answer ID: 3384 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 322/288=B) Ask your mother to recite the below dua seven times: أ س أ ل اللہ العظیم رب العرش العظیم أن یشفینی Also, ask her to recite ­ya slalam ( یا سلام ) as much as she can. (2) There is no need to go for treatment to such a person. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
